why: Inserting the fallback that favors cuts after clause boundaries/punctuation made the scorer prefer punctuation-adjacent cut positions (raising the top-ranked cut frequency — rank_depth Δ at k=1 is +0.737), so it improved many short-piece splits (bins ≤3..≤10) but produced more harmful early/small fragments in long-piece contexts (bin ≤99 went negative) by moving cuts to just after punctuation or clause openings and thereby isolating tiny function-word pieces or separating heads from their complements.
lesson: When adding a punctuation/clause-boundary fallback, constrain it so it does not outrank avoidance of creating very short/leading fragments or splitting a head from its essential post‑nominal/complement material.
